Oh, I'm busy writing the first risk assessment report for the "Unified Data Service Center" project, and I'm almost done. This report needs to be reviewed by all core members. Where should I create it? I think there was a central place for project materials before, but I really don't have time to dig through chat logs right now. Can you help me find it?

Options:
A. It should be created and shared using Feishu Docs. Project Director Mingzhi Li suggested on January 17 that, considering Feishu's deep integration with instant messaging, all reports requiring quick circulation and multi-person feedback should prioritize Feishu Docs to improve collaboration efficiency.
B. It should be uploaded to the company's unified SharePoint portal. According to the latest management regulations issued by the Group PMO on January 20, to comply with company audit requirements, all formal project evaluation reports and milestone documents must be archived to the designated SharePoint site. Yongping Lin has confirmed receipt and requested compliance in the Project Director group chat.
C. Should be created as a Markdown file in the project's GitLab repository. Technical Lead Huilan Chen proposed at the architecture review meeting on January 18 that all project-level design and evaluation documents should be included in GitLab to ensure version synchronization between documentation and project code.
D. It should be created on Confluence. According to the usual practice during the project initiation phase, Yongping Lin has clearly designated Confluence as the unified platform for managing and sharing core project documents (such as meeting agendas and materials), and the new report should follow this standard.
gold: D. It should be created on Confluence. According to the usual practice during the project initiation phase, Yongping Lin has clearly designated Confluence as the unified platform for managing and sharing core project documents (such as meeting agendas and materials), and the new report should follow this standard.

I'm attending the Apache Pulsar technical review meeting tomorrow, and preparing the materials is giving me a headache. To improve the real-time performance of our data services, someone proposed using this new technology for data synchronization and provided an initial report. I remember we had a lot of discussions about this before. To help me focus on the key points, could you remind me what the most critical criteria were when we evaluated this new solution?

Options:
A. The evaluation should be based on the Business Model Canvas finalized by the project team as the core principle. As requested by Mingzhi Li, all technical solution reviews must use this as a benchmark to ensure that technical decisions align with the project's core business objectives.
B. Its technical advancement and performance metrics should be prioritized for evaluation. According to the "Technology Selection Specification V2.1" issued by the company's Technical Committee at the beginning of the year, the introduction of new technologies requires priority consideration of their community activity, performance stress test data, and compatibility with the existing technology stack.
C. The "Unified Messaging Queue (UMQ) Technical Specification" determined by the team at the architecture review meeting on February 10 should be the primary standard. Mingzhi Li explicitly pointed out at that meeting that to avoid technology stack fragmentation, all new business data exchange middleware must be encapsulated based on the team's standardized RocketMQ, and in principle, no new message queue technologies should be introduced.
D. D. Focus should be placed on considering its introduction cost and operation and maintenance complexity. Project lead Weihua Zhang emphasized at the recent budget review meeting that, given limited project resources, any new technical component introduced must be accompanied by a detailed cost-benefit analysis report, and open-source, mature solutions should be prioritized.
gold: A. The evaluation should be based on the Business Model Canvas finalized by the project team as the core principle. As requested by Mingzhi Li, all technical solution reviews must use this as a benchmark to ensure that technical decisions align with the project's core business objectives.

Hey, Xiao Zhu, could you help me check something? For the new data ingestion module in our data analytics portal, we need to finalize the technical solution, and we're currently evaluating several open-source message queues. Just looking at the official documentation isn't enough; we need someone to do a comparative analysis to assess their community activity, industry adoption, and long-term maintenance prospects. Who was assigned to this research task? I'm busy building the framework and really don't have time to dig through chat logs.

Options:
A. Huilan Chen should be personally responsible. She is in charge of the competitor analysis task. Although Chunfang Jiang provided assistance, according to project management conventions, this critical research involving technical selection direction should be completed by the task owner personally to ensure the accuracy of evaluation dimensions and avoid information transfer deviations.
B. It should be assigned to the technical lead, Yu Gu. In the communication with Yu Gu on February 4, Huilan Chen clearly stated that he would lead the subsequent technical evaluations. Community activity and maintenance prospects are core components of technical feasibility assessment and should be thoroughly researched and concluded by the technical side.
C. It should be led by Huilan Chen, with Yu Gu invited to complete it together. At the technical selection kick-off meeting held on February 5, Huilan Chen clarified the new working model: all external technical research must be jointly conducted by the business demand side (Huilan Chen) and the technical implementation side (Yu Gu) to ensure that the evaluation considers both business and technology. Chunfang Jiang's assistance is limited to the previous round of competitor analysis, which has already concluded.
D. It should be handled by Chunfang Jiang. According to the communication on February 3, the team has established a division of labor: Chunfang Jiang proactively took on the task of collecting objective product evaluations and user feedback from external channels such as technical communities and analysis reports, which was confirmed by Huilan Chen. The new task falls within this scope of responsibility.

Ugh, the product team has another task for us. They want to add a user behavior tracking module to the "Data Asset Portal." I'm swamped with bug fixes right now and don't have time to dig through Confluence. Can you check for me what framework we've decided to use for the backend service of this new module?

Options:
A. Java/SpringBoot framework should be used. According to Mingzhi Li's final technology selection decision released to all members on March 7, Java/SpringBoot is the only designated backend technology stack for the "Data Asset Catalog and Analysis Portal" project.
B. Go language should be used. Given that the user behavior tracking module has strict requirements for high concurrency and low latency, the Technical Committee issued supplementary guidelines on March 15 for such high-performance service scenarios, recommending the use of Go language for development to ensure system performance.
C. Node.js should be used. Although Java was initially decided as the main backend technology for the project, considering that the frontend tech stack is React, Mingzhi Li, the technical lead, decided in a special discussion held on March 20 that to achieve isomorphic development for frontend and backend and improve development efficiency, all BFF (Backend for Frontend) layer services that interact closely with the frontend (such as user behavior tracking) will uniformly adopt Node.js for development. This decision has been updated in the Confluence document.
D. Python/Django framework should be adopted. Considering that the core of this module is user behavior analysis, architect Hai Wang specifically pointed out at the technical review meeting on March 10 that the Python ecosystem has obvious advantages in data processing and algorithm integration, making it more suitable for such scenarios, and this has been approved.
gold: A. Java/SpringBoot framework should be used. According to Mingzhi Li's final technology selection decision released to all members on March 7, Java/SpringBoot is the only designated backend technology stack for the "Data Asset Catalog and Analysis Portal" project.

According to the latest Technical Committee regulations from March 25, all cross-service communication protocols, whether synchronous APIs or asynchronous messages, must undergo unified design and approval by the Architecture Group to ensure the technical consistency and scalability of the entire portal system.

She was the original designer of the asynchronous communication solution, and its message structure was adopted as the standard paradigm. To ensure consistency between the new scenario and the original design intent, having her directly define the specific message format for the 'Data Quality Audit' service will ensure the best practice continuity.

I've run into an issue: the Marketing Department wants to add third-party data tags to user profiles, but the Legal Department says there are privacy risks and has put a stop to it. Now the two departments are at a stalemate over data collection boundaries. I'm not sure what our team's usual practice is for handling these kinds of inter-departmental disputes, and who I should approach to mediate and help them reach an agreement.

Options:
A. It should be submitted to Project Director Zhigang Wang for a decision. This issue involves legal and compliance red lines, exceeding the scope of routine business coordination. According to the project charter, all cross-departmental decisions involving significant compliance risks must be escalated to the Project Director level, who will then designate a responsible person or make the final decision directly.
B. It should be handled by Jianguo Huang from the Operations Department. According to the discussion on March 27, when cross-departmental issues arise that require aligning different business units to clarify rules, it was decided that the Operations Department would lead the coordination efforts. The current disagreement between the Marketing Department and the Legal Department is a recurrence of such a scenario, and the established division of labor should be followed.
C. It should be led by Product Manager Yongping Lin. He first discovered this type of cross-departmental rule issue when reviewing the PRD, and the user persona tag design for the new feature itself falls within the scope of product requirements. D. It should be led by the Legal Department, with the Marketing Department assisting. Assistant, quick, help me check something. Our Data Service Center needs to integrate a new enterprise credit inquiry API, and the provider gave us an `AppID` and `AppSecret`. I remember we discussed how to manage this kind of sensitive information before, but I'm busy with joint debugging now and don't have time to dig through meeting minutes. Isn't Haitao Peng working on that configuration center solution? Should he manage these authentication credentials centrally, or did we have a different rule back then?

Options:
A. Should be evaluated by Security Engineer Taoxuan Yu and then stored in a new independent Key Management Service (KMS). At the security special meeting on April 5, the project team reached a consensus that for all external service credentials, an independent KMS will be introduced for unified management to meet higher compliance requirements, and the scattered solutions of individual projects will no longer be used.
B. It should be managed within the final selected Apollo configuration center, utilizing its built-in encryption and authorization features. At the technical solution review meeting on April 10, Lingyun Pan updated her previous preliminary suggestion, pointing out that introducing K8s Secret would increase operational complexity and deployment coupling. The meeting ultimately adopted Haitao Peng's proposal, deciding to use Apollo's namespace isolation and encryption/decryption plugins to uniformly manage all configurations, including sensitive credentials like API keys, to simplify the overall technology stack.
C. A dedicated configuration item should be created in the configuration center for centralized management. Haitao Peng's responsibility is to build a unified configuration solution, incorporating credit credentials into it. This will allow for better utilization of the features he is designing for management by application, environment, and user tags, enabling dynamic updates and grayscale releases.
D. It should be planned to be managed through Kubernetes Secrets. According to the technical principles proposed and adopted by Lingyun Pan, the design of the API Center should strictly differentiate between sensitive and non-sensitive configurations. Credentials for credit reporting interfaces are highly sensitive information and should not be included in the scope of application configuration center management. Instead, more secure, dedicated solutions like Kubernetes Secrets should be used.

Ugh, this is a headache. Product just dropped another urgent request. I need to quickly estimate the workload, no time to dig through Confluence. They want different approval workflows based on data sensitivity levels. For example, 'highly sensitive' data would require approval from both the Data Owner and Legal, while 'general' data only needs one approval. Can you quickly check for me if our current system design can directly support this kind of functionality?

Options:
A. Yes, it can be supported. Based on the design confirmed by Lei Shi on April 11, the system has been developed according to the dynamic approval flow principles proposed by Li Wu. Its database table structure natively supports custom approval nodes and process templates, and can fully meet the requirement of setting different approval paths based on data sensitivity levels.
B. Currently, it's not supported. For V1, to launch quickly, we adopted the fixed approval flow solution suggested by Li Wu. To implement this dynamic assignment, Lei Shi needs to redesign the database table structure and schedule it for phase two development, which is estimated to require at least three weeks of work.
C. Cannot be directly supported. At the technical review meeting on April 10, Project Manager Huilan Chen, considering the pressure of the project timeline, ultimately rejected Li Wu's dynamic solution and decided that all approval workflows would uniformly go through the supervisor of the applicant's department. This new requirement conflicts with the established plan.
D. This requirement needs to be implemented by introducing an external BPMN engine. At the architecture special meeting on April 15, CTO Weiguo Zhao pointed out that handwritten approval flow logic has high maintenance costs, and decided to purchase a third-party process engine and integrate it with the data catalog. Lei Shi's current task has been changed to conduct relevant technical pre-research, rather than extending based on the original design. Therefore, this requirement should be incorporated into the planning of the new engine for unified processing.

query:
Xiao A, I've just started working on the new "cross-database data synchronization" module, and I'm currently stuck on the log design. For information like task start time, end time, and execution status (success/failure), where should I record it? I vaguely recall a similar discussion before, but there are too many chat records to find it. I'd like to double-check with you: does our platform have any established conventions for this type of task log? I want to avoid redundant design.

Options:
A. Should be written into Fanmin Tian's designed rule result table. This is because both data synchronization and data quality validation are platform rule-driven tasks. To ensure the uniformity of the log model, all execution process logs for rule-based tasks should follow Fanmin Tian's existing design specifications for recording.
B. These execution process logs should be written to the general task log table managed by Kai Yuan. According to the consensus reached by Kai Yuan and Fanmin Tian on April 16, execution logs for special tasks within the platform need to be centrally managed to avoid fragmentation, and the newly developed data synchronization module should follow this convention.
C. A dedicated execution log table should be created for the "Cross-database Data Synchronization" module. According to the project architect's recommendation, to ensure complete decoupling and independent iteration between core modules, each task should establish its own closed-loop logging system to avoid over-reliance on general tables.
D. It should be uniformly pushed to the company-level ELK log center. According to the latest specifications released by the Technical Committee on April 25, to enhance the overall observability of the platform, all execution process logs for new modules (including data synchronization) must be output in a standard format to the central log system. Creating independent log tables in the business database is no longer permitted. This decision has been communicated to all developers, including Kai Yuan.
gold: B. These execution process logs should be written to the general task log table managed by Kai Yuan. According to the consensus reached by Kai Yuan and Fanmin Tian on April 16, execution logs for special tasks within the platform need to be centrally managed to avoid fragmentation, and the newly developed data synchronization module should follow this convention.

**B. Write to the general task log table managed by Kai Yuan.**

Hey, assistant, could you quickly take a look at this for me? I'm working on the new 'Message Push Service' and I'm stuck on the retry logic. To speed things up, I want to store the status of recently failed tasks directly in memory, so I don't have to query the database when retrying. I recall there was some rule about this when we discussed high availability. Will doing this cause any problems? Could you double-check it for me?

Options:
A. The solution is feasible, but fallback measures need to be added. For services like message pushing, which have extremely high real-time requirements, using in-memory caching can significantly reduce latency and external dependencies. This design is acceptable as long as recent task states can be recovered from database logs when an instance restarts.
B. This solution is completely feasible. During the in-depth review meeting on high-availability architecture on May 8, Mingzhi Li specifically pointed out that for temporary data with an extremely short lifecycle (minutes) and non-transactional nature, such as push task statuses, caching in service memory is permissible to achieve ultimate performance and low latency. He emphasized that this is a known exception to the "stateless design" principle and has been updated in the latest architecture design specification, v2.1.
C. The solution is not feasible; local disk files should be used for caching. Lingyun Pan further explained in subsequent discussions that to avoid increasing the overall pressure on the Redis cluster, temporary states of non-core functions like push services can be persisted to the container's local disk instead of memory, ensuring data is not lost after a service restart.
D. This solution is not feasible. According to the mandatory specifications established by Mingzhi Li on May 1, all backend services in the API Center must be designed to be stateless. Any session or temporary state data must be externalized to a distributed cache (such as Redis) or a database to ensure high availability.
gold: D. This solution is not feasible. According to the mandatory specifications established by Mingzhi Li on May 1, all backend services in the API Center must be designed to be stateless. Any session or temporary state data must be externalized to a distributed cache (such as Redis) or a database to ensure high availability.

I've looked at it, and the table filtering and sorting requirements for this page are quite complex. I'm about to start the technical selection process, but I'm not sure if there are any recommended or unified standards for complex tables in our project. I'm worried that if I just pick a solution, it might not meet the standards later and I'll have to refactor it.

Zihan Zou reported at the technical sharing session on June 7 that although he had considered reusing Yuxin Su's component, an in-depth evaluation revealed that it had high coupling and lacked virtual scrolling functionality, making it unable to meet the performance requirements for rendering large volumes of log data. Therefore, the team ultimately decided to uniformly switch to the Vxe-Table solution, which offers better performance.
B. It should be a new component developed independently, based on the secondary encapsulation of Element Plus's basic table. Project lead Weihua Zhang emphasized at the project kick-off meeting that to avoid communication and maintenance costs caused by cross-project team dependencies, core components of the admin backend should remain independently developed.
C. The community-popular Ant Design ProTable component should be chosen. At the frontend technology selection meeting on June 6, architect Engineer Li pointed out that this component is powerful, has mature documentation, and can meet the complex interactive requirements for log queries. The team should prioritize adopting mature open-source solutions.
D. D. Directly reuse the table component developed by Yuxin Su from the 'Data Asset Catalog' project team. According to Zihan Zou's discussion on June 5, to unify the technology stack and improve efficiency, all complex list pages in the admin backend project have been confirmed to use this component, and it has already been applied first in the API list page.

Assistant, quick, help me out. Our new 'Membership Points Service' is going live on Sentinel. I was thinking of putting the rule files directly in Git, packaged with the code, for easier management. Should this be okay? I vaguely remember someone mentioning a relevant standard before, but I can't recall it now. Please double-check for me quickly, so it doesn't get rejected after deployment.

Options:
A. Partially compliant, but hardcoding should be used. Although Mingzhi Li requested the gateway to use Nacos in the discussion on June 2, he specifically added at the technical review meeting on June 10: For non-gateway core business services (such as the points service), to reduce operational complexity and external dependencies, hardcoding should be prioritized. After the traffic model stabilizes, a unified assessment should be conducted to determine whether to migrate to Nacos for dynamic management.
B. Does not meet technical specifications. According to the strict requirements previously established by Mingzhi Li, all Sentinel rules in the project must use Nacos for dynamic configuration to facilitate real-time traffic control and degradation strategy adjustments online, avoiding service redeployment.
C. Does not comply with specifications. According to the latest guidelines issued by the architecture team on June 5, to integrate the company's configuration management technology stack, all newly built microservices should uniformly use the internal configuration platform ConfigMaster to manage dynamic rules. Nacos will be gradually archived next quarter.
D. Compliant with specifications and a recommended solution. Versioning Sentinel rules in Git follows the modern DevOps principle of "configuration as code," ensuring strong consistency between configurations and application versions, greatly facilitating environmental auditing and one-click rollbacks.
gold: B. Does not meet technical specifications. According to the strict requirements previously established by Mingzhi Li, all Sentinel rules in the project must use Nacos for dynamic configuration to facilitate real-time traffic control and degradation strategy adjustments online, avoiding service redeployment.

agent_answer:
The correct option is **A**.

**Why:**  
In the June 2 discussion, Mingzhi Li’s “mandatory Nacos” requirement was made in direct response to **Ping Cai’s question about the API Gateway’s Sentinel rules** – it was gateway-scoped, not a blanket rule for every service.

For the **Membership Points Service** (a non-gateway core business service), the governing standard is Mingzhi Li’s Sentinel configuration management specification, which defines the rule management mode as **“code-internal baseline solidification”** – i.e., rules live in/with the code (exactly what Git-packaged rule files achieve), and resources carrying **CRITICAL_RESOURCE_TAG** are **prohibited from being created/overwritten in Nacos**. So hardcoding is prioritized here, with a later unified assessment on whether to migrate to Nacos once the traffic model stabilizes.

- **B** is wrong because “all Sentinel rules must use Nacos” contradicts this later, more specific spec and the gateway/non-gateway distinction.
- **C** has no support in the material (no ConfigMaster / June 5 architecture guidelines appear anywhere).
- **D** overstates the case and ignores the gateway vs. non-gateway nuance established by Mingzhi Li.

So: putting the rule files in Git packaged with the code is acceptable **as long as they are treated as hardcoded baseline rules** – option **A**.

Now the frontend needs to integrate the generic table component that supports sorting and filtering to display the report list. A. Contact Senior Frontend Engineer Haitao Wang. B. Zihan Zou should be responsible for the integration. According to the communication on June 2, the development and integration of the reusable table component have clear divisions of labor. Yuxin Su is responsible for development, and Zihan Zou is confirmed to be responsible for the subsequent integration tasks. The new module should follow this established division of labor.
C. You should directly contact the component developer, Yuxin Su. According to her explanation during the component release on June 3, to ensure the component API is correctly understood and used, she will personally follow up and support the integration work for the first few business pages to collect feedback and improve the documentation.
D. Should be submitted to Li Wei, the head of the front-end architecture team. query:
I'm swamped! The product team just came up with a new request: they want to add a "filter by department" feature to the search function in the "Data Analytics Portal." I asked R&D, and they said it would require modifying the underlying search engine index. I need to quickly find someone to estimate the workload, but I can't remember who's currently maintaining the index. Can you help me find out who I should talk to about this?

Options:
A. Should be submitted to the Data Governance Committee for review. According to the project charter, all changes involving core data models (including search indexes) must go through the formal approval process of this committee to ensure the consistency and standardization of the entire data asset platform, and cannot be decided by individuals without authorization.
B. It should be handled by Lei Shi. She is the developer of the global search API, and the new feature will ultimately be implemented in her API code. From a technical implementation perspective, having her lead the changes to the indexing structure can most effectively ensure consistency between the front-end and back-end definitions and reduce communication costs.
C. It should be fully handled by Lei Shi. Chunfang Jiang only provided initial environmental information on June 26. According to the latest resolution from the API Design Review Meeting on June 28, to ensure accountability, all subsequent index requirement changes strongly related to the search function have been uniformly transferred to Lei Shi, the direct owner of the API, to lead the evaluation and drive modifications. Chunfang Jiang will only serve as a technical support consultant.
D. It should be handled by Chunfang Jiang. As the initial provider of the search engine index mapping, she explicitly committed to taking responsibility for subsequent fine-tuning and synchronization during the communication on June 26. The new feature to filter by department is a typical index structure fine-tuning, so she should continue to be responsible for this.

Hey, Assistant, could you help me out? My new 'Log Analysis Service' is waiting to be deployed to the test environment, and I need to get the K8s deployment files ready quickly. I remember there was a unified specification document and templates for this before, but I'm swamped with work right now and don't have time to look for them. Could you help me find out where I should look?

Options:
A. You should directly look it up in the company's unified Rancher management platform. According to the notice from the new DevOps lead, Hao Chen, on August 1, to achieve standardized and automated environment management, the company has discontinued all document-based specifications. All application deployment templates and resource quotas are now available as standard templates in the Rancher platform's app store, ready for direct use without manual YAML writing.
B. Should be found in the Jira project template. Mingzhi Li explicitly stated at the project weekly meeting on July 20 that, in order to strongly bind deployment requirements with development tasks, the deployment specifications for all new services have been integrated into Jira as a standard sub-task template and will be automatically included when new features are created.
C. Should be found in the GitLab repository's Wiki. According to the resolution of the Technical Architecture Review Meeting on July 15, to achieve the best practice of "documentation as code," all service Kubernetes deployment specifications and YAML templates have been migrated to the respective project's GitLab repository Wiki for centralized management.
D. Should be found in Confluence. According to Mingzhi Li's previous instructions, the team has established a unified Kubernetes deployment specification, and all service deployment templates and configuration standards are stored under the 'DevOps Center' path in Confluence.

Assistant, I've just taken over the data asset portal. I have a question about technology selection. We need to add a new feature that requires parsing Greenplum SQL, mainly to clarify the lineage relationships between tables. I recall our team might have done similar technical research before. For scenarios like SQL parsing to extract lineage, are there any recommended standard solutions or libraries available now?

Options:
A. You should use ANTLR for a custom grammar parser. At the architecture review meeting on July 15, the technical lead pointed out that given the significant differences between Greenplum's SQL dialect and the standard, to ensure parsing accuracy, we should abandon general-purpose libraries and build the parsing logic from the ground up.
B. It is recommended to use the `sqlparse` library. Although it cannot directly extract lineage, it is highly versatile and has an active community. We can develop on top of its parse tree, which will provide better extensibility for supporting more non-standard SQL dialects in the future.
C. `Apache Calcite` should be used as the parsing engine. Haoming Zhu updated the conclusion in his technical sharing on July 20, pointing out that `sqllineage` has limitations when dealing with complex nested views and UDFs. To support more complex data governance requirements in the future in one go, the team decided to switch to Calcite, which is more powerful and has a more complete ecosystem. The relevant PoC verification was completed last week.
D. The `sqllineage` library should be prioritized. According to the technical selection report published by Haoming Zhu on July 11, this library has been identified as the standard tool for the team to parse SQL and extract table-level lineage, and new tasks should adhere to this established standard.
gold: D. The `sqllineage` library should be prioritized. According to the technical selection report published by Haoming Zhu on July 11, this library has been identified as the standard tool for the team to parse SQL and extract table-level lineage, and new tasks should adhere to this established standard.

Xiao A, please help me double-check something. I'm integrating a new 'Credit Approval' microservice, and the compliance requirements are extremely strict, it's giving me a headache. They require that the signature key for identity authentication must be dynamically rotated quarterly. I remember Ping Cai was in charge of gateway authentication before, but I really don't have time to dig through the Confluence design documents. Can our current solution be used directly, or do we need to quickly schedule a time with him for modifications?

Options:
A. The plan has been changed. During the security architecture special meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li on July 25, it was decided to abandon the self-built JWKS solution and uniformly adopt the cloud vendor's KMS service for key management. This solution can better achieve full-link encryption and unified auditing. Ping Cai is currently refactoring the authentication plugin based on the KMS SDK to meet stricter financial compliance standards.
B. Partial support. According to Si-yu Liang's decision at the technical review meeting on July 20, all key information must be uniformly managed by the configuration center. This means the gateway can obtain new keys after a service restart, but it cannot achieve dynamic, seamless hot updates, which does not meet the high availability requirements of the credit service.
C. Not currently supported. The existing solution uses static public key verification, which is stable but cannot be dynamically updated. To meet the compliance requirements for credit services, Ping Cai needs to modify the existing plugin and arrange a dedicated operation and maintenance process to manually update public key files and restart the gateway service regularly.
D. Can be met. According to the gateway authentication plugin design submitted by Ping Cai and confirmed by Mingzhi Li on July 16, the team has adopted the JWKS solution. Xiao Zhu, could you help me with something? I've just taken over our "Unified API Center" project and I'm looking into the permission management. The backend functionality is almost complete, and now I need to add audit logs for user operations. I recall there was a discussion in the group about a unified logging solution that could be implemented with annotations, but I've searched through the chat history and can't find it. Can you help me figure out what the standard approach is now? I don't want to use the wrong method.

Options:
A. You should directly use the `@OpLog` annotation packaged by Li Wu. According to the record from July 23, she has completed the development of a general logging aspect based on AOP, aiming to unify the project's logging implementation and avoid hardcoding coupling between business code and logging logic. New modules only need to add this annotation to the corresponding methods.
B. The log content should be encapsulated as events and sent to a dedicated log center via RocketMQ. This is a new proposal put forward by architect Mingzhi Li at the review meeting on July 25, aiming to completely decouple logs from business systems, improve overall system availability, and increase log processing throughput.
C. Manually record using the static method `LogUtil` provided in the project's base library. This is a standard defined by Kai Yuan in the early stages of the project, requiring explicit calls at critical points in the business logic. Although slightly intrusive, it ensures the flexibility of log recording and the completeness of contextual information.
D. Should be uniformly integrated into the company's ELK logging platform. According to Project Director Mingzhi Li's announcement in the project group on August 1, to achieve unified collection and analysis of cross-system logs, all new modules must use the company's encapsulated `Log-Starter` dependency package. This package automatically collects method information and pushes it to the Kafka cluster, from which Logstash consumes it into Elasticsearch. The old `@OpLog` annotation method is planned for deprecation.

I'd like to know where I should typically post the first draft of this design document for everyone to review and follow up on.

This platform has already been integrated with the project team's permission system.
B. It should be published on the GitLab Wiki. According to the latest regulations from Architect Qiang Li on July 29, to achieve "documentation as code," all design documents closely related to API and code implementation must be managed in the project's GitLab repository Wiki.
C. It should be published on Feishu Docs. Project Manager Yuzhen Deng announced at the weekly meeting on July 30 that to standardize the company's collaboration tools, all new project documentation work will be migrated to the Feishu platform, Confluence will be gradually phased out, and new documents are required to be created on Feishu starting immediately.
D. It should be published on Confluence. Based on Kai Yuan's practice on July 25 and 28, the team has established a routine that all API-related design documents are created, shared, and version-controlled on Confluence to ensure consistency in collaboration.

Hello Assistant, I'm Wei Wang, and I'm new here. I've just taken over the API design for user authentication and authorization for the "Unified Data Service Center." I've noticed that our team's documentation seems a bit disorganized, and I'm not sure about the standards. Could you please help me find out where the initial draft of such an API design proposal is usually placed, according to our team's rules?

Options:
A. It should be placed in Feishu Docs. On August 5, frontend lead Zihan Zou proposed that, considering collaboration efficiency with the frontend team and the convenience of mobile review, all API designs requiring frontend review should primarily use Feishu Docs for sharing.
B. It should be placed in the company's unified SharePoint document library. According to the latest notice issued by Technical Manager Mingzhi Li on August 15, to integrate the company's internal knowledge assets and strengthen access control, the "Unified Data Services" project team completed all document migration from Confluence to SharePoint that week. All new documents must be created in SharePoint.
C. It should be placed in the project's GitLab Wiki. According to the requirements set by Project Lead Weihua Zhang at the kickoff meeting in early August, to achieve the best practice of "documentation as code," all interface-related technical design documents must be version-controlled in the code repository's Wiki.
D. It should be placed on Confluence. Based on XinChen Shi's practice in August when handling the "API Subscription Interface" document, the team has established a convention that all API interface design drafts and final documents are uniformly managed and reviewed on Confluence.

Hey, I need to fast-track something. The product team has a new request: add a feature to the Data Asset Portal to automatically reject access requests that haven't been processed for over 72 hours. I'm currently designing the backend scheduled task for this; logically, it's just a status change, but it feels a bit too simple... I recall there being some specific regulations regarding approval rejections. Could you please confirm this for me?

Options:
A. The core is to add a notification mechanism. After an automatic rejection, the applicant should be informed of the result via email or an in-site message. This is a basic product design requirement to ensure users are promptly aware of changes in their application status and to avoid issues caused by information asymmetry.
B. According to the resolution of the architecture review meeting chaired by Li Wu on August 15, this scenario should not be automatically rejected. The correct handling method is to trigger an escalation process: the system will automatically escalate the overdue application to the approver's direct supervisor and mark it as 'urgent'. This measure aims to ensure that important applications are not missed due to individual oversight, thereby guaranteeing business continuity.
C. The reminder function for approvers should be prioritized. When an application is about to expire (e.g., 24 hours remaining), the system should send a strong reminder to the current approver instead of automatically rejecting it. This was proposed by Yuzhen Deng in a follow-up discussion to reduce unnecessary automatic rejections.
D. Must include logic for automatically filling in rejection reasons. According to the business rules previously established by Yuzhen Deng, all rejection operations require a reason for the applicant to trace. Therefore, when this scheduled task changes the status, it should also automatically record a reason such as "Application not processed within the time limit, automatically rejected by the system."
gold: D. Must include logic for automatically filling in rejection reasons. According to the business rules previously established by Yuzhen Deng, all rejection operations require a reason for the applicant to trace. Therefore, when this scheduled task changes the status, it should also automatically record a reason such as "Application not processed within the time limit, automatically rejected by the system."

Ugh, the product team just came up with another new requirement. They want to add an "Asset Impact Analysis" feature to the Data Asset Portal, which would show which downstream reports are affected if a table changes. I'm swamped with work right now and don't have time to dig through old chat logs. Can you help me figure out, given our team's current division of labor, who would be the most suitable person to lead the design of the tracking algorithm for this feature?

Options:
A. Should be evaluated and designed by Technical Architect Jianguo Wang. Asset impact analysis involves cross-system data flows, and its complexity is higher than a single data lineage query, making it a platform-level core capability. According to the project charter, the design of such new core algorithms needs to be uniformly reviewed and introduced by the architecture team to control technical risks.
B. Should be led by Chunlan Shao. Following the team's established practice in the kinship function development, for new features involving graph traversal algorithms, Chunlan Shao's existing graph algorithm utility classes should be reused, and she should lead the technical solution to ensure technical consistency and development efficiency.
C. It should be submitted to the newly established 'General Capabilities Team' for unified planning. Given Haoming Zhu's successful practice of reusing Chunlan Shao's algorithm, Director Huilan Chen decided to establish this team at the project review meeting on August 18. The team aims to abstract graph computing capabilities such as data lineage and impact analysis into platform-level services. Chunlan Shao has already transferred her graph algorithm utility classes to this team for maintenance, and all subsequent new related requirements should be scheduled and implemented through this team.
D. Should be assigned to Haoming Zhu. He just finished developing the upstream lineage query API and has the most direct experience with the latest applications of graph traversal algorithms and data structures. Assigning it to him will ensure consistency in the technical implementation of new and old features and avoid repeating past mistakes.
gold: B. Should be led by Chunlan Shao. Following the team's established practice in the kinship function development, for new features involving graph traversal algorithms, Chunlan Shao's existing graph algorithm utility classes should be reused, and she should lead the technical solution to ensure technical consistency and development efficiency.

Assistant, could you please help me check something? Our new "User Behavior Analysis Report" for the analytics portal is about to enter testing, right? This report contains a lot of sensitive user privacy data, so the test cases for permissions and privilege escalation need to be designed very carefully, otherwise, there could be serious problems. I'm swamped with work right now. I recall we had an agreement on testing responsibilities before, didn't we? Who should be responsible for this kind of security-related testing?

Options:
A. Should be reassigned by Test Lead Chen. According to his latest decision at the special security meeting on August 20, all testing tasks involving Class A user sensitive data must deviate from the regular division of labor model. He will assess the risks and then assign a specialist with a security certification background to follow up, in order to establish an independent audit and verification process.
B. B. This should be a joint responsibility of Haoran Shi and Weibo Qiu. This task has dual attributes: functionality (different permissions correspond to different functional points) and security (preventing unauthorized access). It should be designed collaboratively by both individuals, with Haoran Shi leading the functional verification and Weibo Qiu supplementing the security boundary scenarios to ensure comprehensive coverage.
C. It should be Hao-ran Shi who is responsible. The ultimate manifestation of permission verification is at the functional level, requiring verification of whether the functional interfaces and data fields seen by different roles meet expectations. This falls within the scope of functional test case design for which Hao-ran Shi is responsible.
D. Weibo Qiu should be responsible. According to the testing division of labor established by the team on August 18, Weibo Qiu's responsibilities clearly cover the design of test cases for performance, security, and abnormal scenarios, and anti-privilege escalation testing falls within the core scope of security testing.

Assistant, could you help me with something? I've just finished writing the data desensitization filter and now I need to add monitoring for metrics like processing rate and success rate. I recall our team has a standard approach for selecting monitoring systems for new components, right? I'm a bit pressed for time and don't have a chance to dig through the documentation. Could you tell me which one I should integrate with?

Options:
A. Should be integrated with Datadog. According to the CTO office resolution forwarded by Mingzhi Li on August 25, to unify the technology stack and improve troubleshooting efficiency, the company has fully procured Datadog as its unified monitoring solution. All new projects must integrate with Datadog starting immediately, and the existing Prometheus clusters will be gradually decommissioned next quarter. The relevant migration work has been initiated and led by the SRE team.
B. Should be integrated with Prometheus. According to the conversation on August 21, Ping Cai's solution for integrating the rate limiting plugin with Prometheus was explicitly approved by the person in charge, Mingzhi Li. This has become the de facto monitoring technical standard for the team when developing new components.
C. It should be integrated into the company's self-developed "Tianjing" monitoring platform. Mingzhi Li specifically emphasized at Monday's architecture review meeting that for data security and deep integration with the internal alert platform, all components involved in core business data processing must use the internal "Tianjing" system.
D. Should be integrated into Zabbix. According to the specifications released by the operations team in early August, all core metrics for the company's new services must be uniformly integrated into the Zabbix monitoring platform to facilitate centralized management and alerting by the SRE team. Ping Cai's previous plugin was a temporary solution and will also need to be migrated later.

Assistant, could you help me check something? I'm currently working on the content publishing feature for the API Center, and I'm a bit pressed for time. The PRD only specifies how to filter common sensitive words, but it doesn't mention what to do if a user's post title contains a competitor's brand name (e.g., 'XX Cloud'). Should the backend directly block it, or should it be marked for review first? I don't recall this logic ever being defined. Who should I consult to make a decision on this?

Options:
A. This issue should be submitted to Weihua Zhang, the head of the newly established "Risk Control Strategy Group," for a decision. According to the resolution from the project weekly meeting on August 28, all ambiguous areas involving content safety, anti-cheating, and business rules are no longer to be defined by individual product managers. Instead, they must be uniformly reported to this strategy group for cross-departmental evaluation to ensure compliance. Taoxuan Yu must also follow this process.
B. A review meeting should be organized with product, development, and testing teams to discuss this. Because content review logic involves multiple stages, a single role cannot fully cover its impact. It is necessary to bring together relevant stakeholders to jointly agree on a solution that meets business needs and is easy to implement technically.
C. The initial proposal should be put forward by developer Xinchen Shi. When developing the 'Update Profile' feature, she proactively identified and reported similar logical gaps. She has a deep understanding of these edge cases, so she can first provide technical recommendations, which can then be confirmed by the product team.
D. D. Taoxuan Yu should be responsible for making the decision. According to the team's established practice for handling "nickname occupancy" issues, when business logic not clearly defined in the PRD is encountered during development, she is responsible for defining unified business rules and updating the documentation to ensure product logic consistency.

Hey Assistant, could you help me out? I just took over the data portal, and I've seen user feedback saying that the lineage graph has too many nodes and the relationships are too messy, making it hard to quickly pinpoint information. I'm planning to add a filtering function, for example, by business domain or data table keywords. But the problem now is, what should this filter panel look like, what specific items can be filtered within it, and who should I talk to to confirm these requirements? I checked the records, and it seems like Yongping Lin and Zihan Zou were mainly working on this before. I'm new here and not familiar with things, so I'm a bit lost.

Options:
A. Confirm with Yongping Lin. Based on previous division of labor, Yongping Lin is responsible for the product requirements of this component, including interaction details (to be aligned with PRD) and specific field content to be displayed within the interface. The new filtering function falls within his scope of responsibility.
B. It should be Zihan Zou, the development lead, who first drafts the technical and design proposal. As the implementer of this module, Zihan Zou is most familiar with the existing logic. Having him design it first ensures the technical feasibility of the solution, and then it can be submitted to the product team for review. This is standard practice for the team's agile development.
C. It should be led by Zihan Zou, who will design and submit the proposal. According to the latest resolution from the project weekly meeting on September 5, to improve iteration efficiency, all subsequent functional optimizations and detailed adjustments for the Lineage Diagram have been fully entrusted to Zihan Zou. Yongping Lin will only participate in the final pre-launch acceptance phase and will no longer be involved in the specific design process.
D. Consult with designer Fei Wang from the UI/UX team. To ensure consistency in the visual and interactive experience across the entire data analysis portal, all new UI components, especially common controls like the filter panel, must first have standard design drafts produced by the designer that comply with design specifications.
gold: A. Confirm with Yongping Lin. Based on previous division of labor, Yongping Lin is responsible for the product requirements of this component, including interaction details (to be aligned with PRD) and specific field content to be displayed within the interface. The new filtering function falls within his scope of responsibility.

To ensure the design aligns with the team's overall direction and avoids a messy outcome, what should be my first step before officially starting? Are there any unwritten rules or recommended practices within our team for this?

B. Research mainstream open-source log collectors (e.g., Flume, Logstash) in the industry and produce a competitive analysis report. C. A detailed design document should be prepared first and submitted to Project Manager Mingzhi Li for review. Mingzhi Li emphasized at the project kickoff meeting that all new functional modules must have a reviewed detailed design plan before development to avoid rework risks later on.
D. You should proactively contact Ping Cai and Haoming Zhu, communicate with them, and refer to existing collector implementations. According to Mingzhi Li's previous request, the team needs to learn from each other when developing new collectors to unify design patterns and ensure the continuity of technical solutions.

Could you please double-check this for me? I'm in a hurry to release it. The authentication module refactoring for the Data Service Center is just finished. I ran a code scan on the test branch, and there are no new bugs or security vulnerabilities. The unit test coverage has also reached 82%. Can I merge this directly into the main branch now?

Options:
A. Can be merged. Mingzhi Li finalized the tiered quality gate strategy at the architecture review meeting on October 8: core transaction link code requires 90% coverage, while supporting modules like user authentication have a gate standard of "no new Bugs/Vulnerabilities and coverage no less than 80%". This branch's 82% coverage already meets the release conditions.
B. Can be merged. At the project weekly meeting on September 30, QA Lead Lei Zhang proposed that for support modules of non-core businesses, the test coverage gate can be appropriately relaxed to 80%. The authentication module is a foundational underlying component and is applicable to this exemption clause, so it can be merged.
C. Can be merged. Given that the code does not introduce new bugs or vulnerabilities, it indicates that the core quality is guaranteed. The 82% coverage is not far from the 85% target. It can be merged first to ensure project progress, and then a technical debt task can be arranged later to supplement the test cases.
D. Cannot merge. According to the Quality Gate standards configured by Hantong Wang and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, the unit test coverage for all new code must be no less than 85%. The current coverage of 82% does not meet this hard requirement, so additional test cases are needed.

query:
Oh, this "Data Asset Catalog and Analytics Portal" project is finally coming to an end; it's been exhausting. My boss told me to quickly write up the project post-mortem summary to document the lessons learned. Where do these summaries usually get published? Do we have a centralized place for these kinds of documents? I really don't have time to dig through old records, can you please help me find out?

Options:
A. It should be published on Confluence. According to Wei Du's announcement when the UAT preparation was completed, the final versions of important project deliverables (such as the "UAT Data Usage Guide") are all published on Confluence, which has become the team's established document management standard.
B. Should be created on GitLab Wiki. Huiwei Du suggested in a subsequent technical sharing session that, to achieve the best practice of "documentation as code," documents closely related to technical implementation, such as project retrospectives, should be stored in GitLab along with the project's code repository.
C. It should be published on the company's unified SharePoint portal. According to the latest regulations issued by the IT department in early November, all final project archival materials (especially review reports for cross-departmental sharing) must be uploaded to the SharePoint knowledge base to comply with the group's information security and long-term archiving requirements. Confluence is only to be used for in-progress documentation.
D. It should be published on Feishu Docs. Project Manager Weihua Zhang explicitly stated at the project kick-off meeting that, for convenient mobile review and commenting, all project-level summary documents should be stored uniformly in Feishu Cloud Space for easy access at any time.
gold: A. It should be published on Confluence. According to Wei Du's announcement when the UAT preparation was completed, the final versions of important project deliverables (such as the "UAT Data Usage Guide") are all published on Confluence, which has become the team's established document management standard.

Hey, there's an API performance issue with the API Center project, and the client has been chasing us several times. We need to optimize it quickly. I've looked into it, and adding a Redis secondary cache should do the trick. I've already finished the code and pushed it to the branch. I think I can just submit a PR and merge it, right? For a small optimization like this, we probably don't need to go through the review process again; it's too slow.

Options:
A. According to project regulations, direct PR merges are not allowed. Mingzhi Li has previously made it clear that all technical solutions must undergo a formal review before implementation, and this review must be based on the project's final "Business Model Canvas" to ensure that technical decisions align with the project's strategic foundation. Please prepare the solution document and initiate the review first.
B. Before merging to the main branch, please provide a detailed performance test report. You need to compare the interface response time (RT), throughput (QPS), and CPU utilization before and after adding the cache to ensure that this change indeed brings significant optimization and does not introduce new performance bottlenecks. The report must be confirmed by Test Lead Tao Zhou before proceeding with the merge.
C. You can directly submit a PR. Boss Weihua Zhang, the project lead, emphasized at the latest project weekly meeting on February 5 that to accelerate iteration speed, similar technical optimizations can go through a fast track as long as they don't introduce new paid components. You just need to state in the PR description that Redis reuses existing clusters and incurs no new costs, and simultaneously @Mingzhi Li and himself. Once they confirm online, it can be merged.
D. According to the project team's latest resolution on February 3, all core architecture changes (such as introducing new middleware) must first be submitted to the Architecture Committee for special review. Please fill out the "Architecture Change Request Form" first. Committee Chairman Lei Sun will organize a meeting every Wednesday for discussion, and changes can only be merged after approval.

Xiao A, the Unified Data Service Center project is being rushed. I just read the API Gateway Selection Report sent by Huilan Chen. Apigee's on-premise deployment is too heavy, and operations definitely can't handle it. I see that our operations team is very familiar with Kong, and its performance is also sufficient. Let's just use Kong to get the project going and ensure it can be launched as soon as possible. As for the portal experience, let's put it aside for now and optimize it later. This solution shouldn't be a problem, right?

Options:
A. This proposal has been approved. Director Jianguo Huang himself participated in the discussion at yesterday's (February 14) project decision meeting. Considering the deployment complexity and long-term operational burden of Apigee, it was ultimately decided to use Kong. Regarding the portal experience issue, the meeting decided that the front-end team would develop an independent portal based on an open-source project, and Jing Li has been assigned to lead this, with a prototype planned within one month. This decision has been recorded in the meeting minutes.
B. I agree with you. At the budget review meeting on February 12, the finance department explicitly asked us to prioritize open-source or low-cost solutions, and Apigee's licensing fees are too high. All things considered, Kong is indeed the optimal choice at this stage and meets our cost control requirements.
C. Yes. The CTO's office issued guidelines for technology stack unification on February 11, requiring new projects to prioritize cloud-native architecture and toolchains familiar to our tech department. Kong can seamlessly integrate with our existing monitoring and alerting system, which aligns with these guidelines.
D. This plan is probably not appropriate. Boss Huang repeatedly emphasized at the project kickoff that the developer portal experience is the "top priority" for evaluation, and even the key to whether the API Center project can be successfully promoted. We cannot sacrifice this core strategic objective for the sake of short-term launch speed and operational convenience.

Assistant, the 'data lineage analysis' module is a bit urgent, I need to get started on it right away. Python is clearly much faster than Java for graph computing and data parsing in this area. To speed things up, I'm planning to go directly with Python/Django. Could you please double-check if there are any restrictions on this technology choice for our project?

Options:
A. This proposal is feasible. According to the Architecture Committee's review resolution on March 15, to achieve 'efficiency improvement and cost reduction,' the project has been adjusted to a hybrid technology stack strategy. For data processing and algorithm-intensive modules, Python/Django is explicitly recommended, while business process-oriented modules will maintain Java/SpringBoot. The relevant resolution has been updated in the Confluence document "Data Asset Portal Technical Specification V1.2".
B. Agree. Given the unique nature of the 'Data Lineage Analysis' module, its algorithm-intensive characteristics indeed make Python a more suitable choice. It can be developed as an independent microservice using Python/Django and interact with other Java services via API. Please note this as a technical exception in the proposal.
C. This solution is not feasible. According to the final technical selection decision previously issued by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, the backend technology stack for our "Data Asset Portal" project has been uniformly determined to be Java/SpringBoot, and all new module development should adhere to this specification.
D. Python's GIL issue can lead to performance bottlenecks in high-concurrency scenarios. According to the technical supplementary discussion on March 10, for compute-intensive services, it is recommended to prioritize Go language, as its concurrency model is superior. It is suggested that you research solutions using the Go/Gin framework.
gold: C. This solution is not feasible. According to the final technical selection decision previously issued by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, the backend technology stack for our "Data Asset Portal" project has been uniformly determined to be Java/SpringBoot, and all new module development should adhere to this specification.

Xiao Meng, the user relationship graph module for the Data Asset Portal is scheduled for development next week, so I need to finalize the plan soon. I spent the weekend stress-testing several graph databases and found that NebulaGraph's concurrent query performance absolutely crushes Neo4j. For long-term considerations, I think we should directly use NebulaGraph for this new module. There's no need to stick with older technologies. Could you please double-check this for me? If there are no issues, I'll proceed with this plan.

Options:
A. This is a good proposal. Haoming Zhu also confirmed at the technical sharing session on March 15 that for new modules with high performance requirements, NebulaGraph can be piloted, while old modules will remain on Neo4j. You can continue to advance this plan.
B. The proposal does not align with the project's established technical specifications. According to Director Mingzhi Li's final decision issued on March 10, the Data Asset Portal project has definitively adopted Neo4j as its graph database. This decision was made after comprehensively considering the ecosystem, documentation maturity, and team integration costs.
C. According to Director Mingzhi Li's final instructions at the project quarterly planning meeting on April 2, the graph database selection has been updated. The meeting concluded that although Neo4j was initially favored, considering the significant advantages of NebulaGraph's new version in distributed architecture and cloud-native compatibility, and the vendor's commitment to providing enterprise-level support, it was decided to migrate the project's overall technology stack to NebulaGraph. Neo4j will only be retained for historical data analysis.
D. An update needs to be shared: the decision to use Neo4j has been revised at the architecture review meeting at the end of March. Considering future operation and maintenance costs and community activity, Weihua Zhang, head of the architecture team, suggested and decided that the project will uniformly switch to NebulaGraph going forward.

AI Assistant, the frontend team for the API Center project is really pushing us. To help them start integration testing sooner, I've thought of a solution: I'll deploy the interactive Swagger documentation first, and put off the security authentication part until the next iteration. Can you double-check for me? There shouldn't be any rules against this, right? I want to get this scheduled for them quickly.

Options:
A. In principle, it's not recommended, but it can be used as a temporary solution. Previously, in the Member Center project, Boss Chen approved a similar solution: launching the documentation first, with the authentication part secured by internal VPN access, which accelerated the development efficiency of the front-end and back-end separation. We can refer to this precedent.
B. This solution is feasible and supported by new guidelines. At last week's technical architecture review meeting, Mingzhi Li clearly stated that to improve agile development efficiency, it is permissible to use internally issued one-time tokens to temporarily replace OAuth2 in development and testing environments. This allows for the release of interactive documents to accelerate joint debugging, while also ensuring basic security through short-lived tokens. OAuth2 can then be uniformly enforced in the pre-production environment.
C. This solution is not feasible. According to the established technical principles of the Data Service Center, interactive API documentation and the gateway's authentication and authorization functions must be launched simultaneously. Providing interactive documentation without security protection is equivalent to exposing a "naked" API, which poses serious security risks and is not allowed.
D. Yes. Given the tight project schedule, we can temporarily use an IP whitelist mechanism. We'll add the IP addresses of the frontend integration environment to the gateway whitelist. This will allow them to access the interactive documentation while keeping the risk to a minimum. We can then switch to formal OAuth2 authentication in the next iteration.
gold: C. This solution is not feasible. According to the established technical principles of the Data Service Center, interactive API documentation and the gateway's authentication and authorization functions must be launched simultaneously. Hey, could you double-check something for me? For the unified data service center we're building, the user points section is experiencing some performance pressure. To speed things up, I'm thinking of having the 'Points Service' directly read data from the 'Order Service' replica database, bypassing all those API calls. This should definitely improve performance by an order of magnitude. I think we should just go with this; it's the most efficient way. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right?

Options:
A. Yes, but with preconditions. Considering performance is a key metric, you can connect to the read-only replica of the order service. However, it must be explicitly commented in the code that this is a temporary optimization, and database connection pool monitoring needs to be increased to prevent connection exhaustion.
B. This solution is inconsistent with the established architecture. According to the final version of the 'Unified Data Service Center' V2.0 architecture diagram published by Mingzhi Li, the core service boundaries and interaction protocols have been solidified. To ensure clear system structure and decoupling, direct cross-boundary database access between services is not permitted.
C. Direct connection is not recommended. A better solution is for the DBA team to configure an ETL task in early April to extract order data into the points service's local table every night. This achieves data decoupling and meets near real-time performance requirements.
D. Yes, this proposal has already been discussed and approved. At the performance optimization special meeting on April 15, Mingzhi Li explicitly stated that for the core transaction link, optimization through establishing a 'direct data connection channel' is permitted after reporting to the Architecture Committee. Your suggestion aligns with this resolution. Please add a brief design on Confluence and copy the Architecture Committee to proceed.

Hey, the user profiling service I just took over needs to go live urgently, and I'm stuck on the database configuration. To make things easier and allow for quick switching between development, testing, and production environments, I plan to put the MySQL connection string (the one with the username and password) directly into our configuration center. I remember Haitao Peng and others discussed this before, so this solution should be fine, right? Could you double-check it for me, just to make sure I don't mess it up later?

Options:
A. According to Lingyun Pan's later clarification, for the convenience of development and testing, non-production environment database connection information can be placed in the configuration center. However, production environment connection information must still be strictly managed through K8s Secrets. Therefore, your solution is permissible in Dev/Test environments.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the specifications previously determined by the project team, the configuration center is only used to manage non-sensitive application configurations such as API whitelists and rate limiting thresholds. Sensitive information containing passwords, such as database connection strings, must be managed through K8s Secrets to ensure security.
C. This proposal needs adjustment. According to the technical architecture review meeting resolution chaired by Architect Wang on April 3, the project team ultimately selected Nacos as the unified configuration center. The meeting clarified that all configurations (including database connections) will be managed by Nacos, but sensitive information must be processed using the Nacos-KMS encryption plugin and configured with an independent permission approval workflow. This plan has been recorded in the meeting minutes, aiming to achieve comprehensive centralization of configurations.
D. The solution is feasible. Considering the need to support grayscale releases later, it is recommended to use Apollo uniformly. You can store the connection string in Apollo and enable its built-in encryption function. This ensures storage security and facilitates unified management of multi-environment configurations.

Hey, Xiao A, something needs to be decided quickly. The user authentication module in the API Center currently queries Redis every time under high concurrency, and I'm a bit concerned about its performance. To prepare for next week's stress test, I plan to store user session information directly in the service's local memory. This will definitely improve response speed. This change is minimal and most efficient. I recall that the previous architectural specifications didn't restrict this, right? Could you quickly review it for me? If there are no issues, I'll schedule it.

Options:
A. The solution is generally feasible, but a synchronization mechanism needs to be added. Sessions can be cached in local memory, and a lightweight gRPC service can be introduced to synchronize session state changes between nodes. This approach ensures high performance and resolves single-point issues through eventual consistency. This is a common optimization technique in distributed systems.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the mandatory specifications established by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, all backend services in the API Center must be designed to be stateless to achieve high availability. This means that all stateful data, including user sessions, must be externalized to a distributed cache or database and cannot be stored in the local memory of service instances.
C. This optimization approach is excellent. While the standard requirement is statelessness, for core, high-frequency scenarios like authentication, you can apply for an architectural exception. You need to submit a detailed performance evaluation report to Lingyun Pan, the head of the Architecture Committee, demonstrating that the benefits of local caching far outweigh the risks of introducing state. Once she approves it, you can proceed with implementation.
D. The solution is feasible. This is the latest architecture guideline. At the performance optimization special meeting on May 10, Mingzhi Li himself supplemented the original specification: for read-heavy, write-light scenarios such as user authentication, a hybrid mode of "bounded local cache + event bus" is allowed. This means caching sessions locally while synchronizing session change events via a message queue, balancing extreme performance with eventual consistency. The relevant design template has been published on Confluence.

The correct choice is **D**.

Why: Project Lead **Mingzhi Li** has consistently set the security redline for this project. On 2025-05-14 he said: **"GitHub Secrets is the right direction. Make sure not to expose any sensitive information in the codebase."** (raw excerpt [1]), and earlier on 2025-03-17: **"sensitive information like keys and certificates... cannot be stored in plain text in the Git repository"** (raw excerpt [2]). **Ruixia Lv** herself is also researching how to manage deployment keys securely via GitHub Secrets (raw excerpt [3], [4]). So writing a temporary API key directly into the config file — even temporarily — violates this explicit redline, and the memory confirms GitHub Secrets as the sanctioned approach.

The other options do not match the record:

- **A** attributes the HashiCorp Vault recommendation to Mingzhi Li, but in the material it was **Siyu Liang** who suggested Vault/Secrets Managers (raw excerpt [5]); Mingzhi Li endorsed GitHub Actions/IRSA, not a decision to switch to Vault.
- **B** claims frontend lead **Xinchen Shi** suggested a `.env.local` approach — there is no record of Xinchen Shi making such a suggestion.
- **C** contradicts Mingzhi Li's explicit prohibition on exposing sensitive information in the codebase.

query:
Assistant, I'm working on user authentication for the data asset portal. During joint debugging, I have to log in again every time I refresh the page, which is too inefficient. I'm thinking of just putting the Access Token in localStorage; that would make debugging much easier. I've decided to go with this approach. Could you double-check it for me? There shouldn't be any major issues, right? I'm planning to submit the code soon.

Options:
A. It is recommended to use `sessionStorage`. Although it also gets cleared when the page is closed, it is more stable than memory and more secure than `localStorage`, aligning with the latest frontend security baseline. This was the compromise solution proposed by Siyu Liang at last week's security review meeting.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the security policy previously established by Mingzhi Li, the Access Token must be stored in memory to mitigate security risks, while the Refresh Token is transmitted via an httpOnly cookie. Please ensure development adheres to this specification.
C. According to the latest architecture review resolution on May 15, we have abandoned the traditional Token storage solution. The new standard is to use a BFF layer for session proxying, with the frontend only retaining a business-agnostic Session ID in an httpOnly Cookie, completely avoiding the risk of frontend Token leakage. You can directly reuse the relevant code from the API Center project, and Ruixia Lv can provide support.
D. Yes, but for security, the Access Token must be symmetrically encrypted before being stored in localStorage, and the key should be dynamically issued by the backend. This approach facilitates debugging while meeting basic security requirements. Zihan Zou implemented this method in the previous development platform project.

**B.** This solution is not feasible under the project’s established security policy.

According to **Mingzhi Li’s** previously set policy, the **Access Token must be stored in memory**, and the **Refresh Token should be transmitted via an httpOnly cookie**. Putting the Access Token in `localStorage` would violate that policy and increase the risk of token leakage.

The proper approach is to use the existing refresh-token mechanism — when the Access Token expires, the frontend calls `/refresh_token` to silently obtain a new token, which should avoid the need to log in again on every page refresh.
